messages:
ingrid.lopez: Hey support — customer on Dedicated pool 'redwood-prod-us' is intermittently getting routed to eu-west-1. They report 2–3s latency spikes and duplicate billing on long streaming calls. They sent request id 8f3a2c7b and say their SDK is using hedged requests. Can we triage?

support-bot: Created ticket INC-4921 for this thread and assigned to @sam.choi :white_check_mark:

sam.choi: Looking now. Can you paste the client's SDK config + a small excerpt of their client logs (no PII)? Also any trace/span id would help.

ingrid.lopez: Here's the minimal config they shared: ```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  region: 'auto',
  hedgedRequests: true,
  maxHedge: 2,
  timeoutMs: 12000,
  retryBackoff: { type: 'exponential', jitter: 'full' }
});
```
And a trimmed log (timestamps are ms):
```
[2024-05-03T12:01:02.123Z] SEND id=8f3a2c7b -> endpoint=api.us-west-2.redwood.com
[2024-05-03T12:01:02.278Z] HEDGE id=8f3a2c7b -> endpoint=api.eu-west-1.redwood.com (hedge #1)
[2024-05-03T12:01:04.900Z] RESP id=8f3a2c7b <- api.eu-west-1.redwood.com status=200 time=2622ms
[2024-05-03T12:01:04.902Z] RESP id=8f3a2c7b <- api.us-west-2.redwood.com status=200 time=2779ms
```
They say both upstreams consumed GPU time and they were billed for it.

sam.choi: That log nails it. Two nearly-concurrent upstreams for same logical request. Short answer: hedgedRequests + "auto" region selection + slow primary path = simultaneous hedges across regions. Two problems we should fix: (1) hedged branch not propagating a stable client-assigned request id header (X-Redwood-Req) so backend treats them as separate billable requests; (2) hedged branch not adding a region-affinity header so router sometimes sends hedge to different region endpoint instead of local fallback.

chris: I pulled router logs for request 8f3a2c7b. Confirmed behavior: when DNS lookup for primary exceeds 150ms, the hedger spawns hedges using endpoint discovery which returns prioritized region list and we currently pick fallback at index 1 without copying the request-id header. Also the hedged-path code intentionally allowed different endpoints to increase success probability — but we didn't attach a shared logical-id header.

chris: P0 short-term mitigations we can recommend to customers: set hedgedRequests=false (or maxHedge=0) OR pin region to a specific region (region: 'us-west-2') OR set regionalAffinity: 'sticky' in client config. This avoids cross-region hedges until we ship a patch.

maria_g: Repro steps I used in staging to match their logs: 1) start a long streaming generate (10s) against a non-cold model on us-west-2; 2) introduce artificial DNS delay (iptables/delay) for us-west-2 ~180ms; 3) client with hedgedRequests:true + region:'auto' will open primary + hedge to eu-west-1, both get scheduled on different GPU pools. I captured router traces and backend allocation ids.

maria_g: Quick detection rule for billing team: if we receive two upstream allocations within 500ms with same original client start timestamp but different internal allocation ids, flag for potential duplicate-billing due to hedges. I can dump a query for billing if you want.

ingrid.lopez: Customer requests a refund for the duplicate GPU usage and wants a timeline for a permanent fix. Can we commit to an ETA?

sam.choi: Engineering plan: (A) Patch hedger to always forward X-Redwood-Req and X-Region-Affinity when spawning hedges (PR inbound), (B) ensure hedges reuse same logical request id so backend can do de-dup/charge attribution, (C) ship SDK patch 1.4.3 that also defaults maxHedge=0 for auto region mode. I'm assigning to @chris to own router + hedger change. Estimated ETA: hotfix branch + deploy to staging in 48 hours, prod rollout in 5 business days pending testing.

chris: Confirmed. I have a small unit test failing in the fallback picker; fixing now. Will add integration test that asserts X-Redwood-Req header present on hedges.

maria_g: Billing: I've opened internal billing ticket BILL-1127 asking for manual review of allocations for request id 8f3a2c7b and a customer refund if both allocations show full billable time. Tagging @finance.

ingrid.lopez: For the customer workaround I'm going to tell them: set hedgedRequests=false or pin region, and we'll escalate a refund investigation.

sam.choi: Also practical short-term SDK workaround we can provide in code: ```js
// customer-recommended temporary config
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  region: 'us-west-2',
  hedgedRequests: false, // disable until patch
  retryBackoff: { type: 'exponential', jitter: 'decorrelated' },
});
```

ingrid.lopez: Perfect. I'll send that to the customer and include the INC-4921 ticket link. Thanks :thumbsup:

chris: FYI, after patch we'll add a router metric exposing hedged-created-per-request so SRE/Support can alert when hedged rate spikes.

maria_g: I'll follow up with billing once they complete the query.

sam.choi: I'll update this thread when the staging hotfix is ready for validation.

ingrid.lopez: Closing loop with customer after you confirm staging results. CC @maria_g for billing.

support-bot: Ticket INC-4921 updated: status=investigating, owner=sam.choi
